test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 11 Aug, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Net domestic product is calculated as _________.

options.text: GDP - Net income earned from abroad
GNP - Net income earned from abroad

solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP - Depreciation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net domestic product** (NDP) is the **total value of goods and services** produced within a country's borders, **minus the depreciation **of capital goods.
 
• **Depreciation** is the **decrease in value of an asset **over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
 
• **GDP - Depreciation** is the correct answer because it** subtracts** the amount of capital goods that have been consumed or used up in the production process from the gross domestic product (GDP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GNP - Depreciation **is incorrect because it** subtracts** the amount of capital goods used up in the production process from the** gross national product (GNP)**, which measures the total value of goods and services produced by a** country's residents,** regardless of their location.
 
• **Gross domestic product **(GDP) is the total value of goods and services produced within a **country's borders, **regardless of the nationality of the producers.
 
• **Gross national product** (GNP) is the** total value of goods and services** produced by a country's residents, regardless of their location.
 
• **Net income earned from abroad** is the **difference** between the income earned by a country's residents from **abroad **(such as from foreign investments or employment) and the income earned by **foreigners** within the country.
 
• **Depreciation** is an important factor to consider in **calculating NDP** because it reflects the **decrease **in the value of capital goods over time and the need for reinvestment in new capital goods to maintain or increase production levels.
